newsitem.title: USA: World wheat stocks better, but still precarious.
newsitem.headline: World wheat stocks better, but still precarious.

text.p: World wheat supplies are more plentiful currently due to unexpected production increases outside the United States, but the global wheat supply picture is still precarious, a major U.S. wheat group said Wednesday.
"We're still in a very precarious situation," said Gregg Doud, marketing analyst for the U.S. Wheat Associates.

"All it is still going to take is one problem in any major wheat producing region of the world" to return to a situation where global wheat consumption is greater than production, Doud said in a briefing on the world wheat outlook.
Doud estimated that 75 percent of this past year's increase in wheat production has been due to good weather, and the remainder to high prices.
"This shows that we're still skating on thin ice," Doud said with regards to the wheat supply situation.

Doud said that U.S. wheat ending stocks could also tighten from USDA's current 435 million bushel estimate due to increased feed use. The analyst said projections may not be adjusted in Thursday's USDA supply/demand report, but said to look for adjustments in January's quarterly stocks report.
